To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a light non-monotonomic knowledge-base is a good approach to support service robots in practical scenarios.

a light KB-system for service robots is presented, where the KB is a hierarchy with inheritance that allows the expression of defaults, exceptions and non-monotonicity, that is embedded within a cognitive architecture, where the KB-system supports the interpretation of the world and the communication with the world.
a non-monotonic conceptual KB can be implemented and used in practical applications in service robotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a KB-System that can be used in a practical service robotics context, where non-monotonicity and dynamic updates are required.
the representation and management of a KB in service robots, which is a crucial component of the overall cognitive architecture.
the development of a light non-monotonical KB-system that is suitable for the practical applications in service and domestic robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first time that a non-monotonic system is embedded in a cognitive architecture for a practical application in service robotics.
the proposed KB-System provides a solid foundation for the implementation of a Non-Monotonics Knowledge-Base for Service Robots.
the proposed KB-System is a practical solution for the representation of non-monotonic and dynamic knowledge in service robots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to provide a practical non-monontonic KB-System that can be embedded in a robot’s architecture and used for service robots scenarios.

we have developed a non-monotonic Knowledge Base for Service Robots that is embedded in an architecture that allows for a coherent and consistent integration of the different kinds of knowledge required for the robot’s behavior.
we have developed a light KB-System that supports non-monotony in service robot applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a practical non-monontonic KB is required for service robots, and that it can be efficiently implemented in a service robot.

a practical non-monontonic KB can be defined in a structured and systematic way and that it can be embedded in the cognitive architecture of a service robot in order to support non-monotonic reasoning in the context of the interaction with the world.
non-monotonicity and defaults are essential for service robots.
